title: Solitary waves and vortices in a Nonlinear Schrödinger equation with ponderomotive nonlinearity
authors: D. K. Campbell, J. Cuevas-Maraver, R. Goh, P. G. Kevrekidis
abstract: In the present work we revisit a ponderomotive nonlinearity model used to examine self-trapped laser beams in plasma. Upon briefly considering the exact stationary 1D solutions of the model, we extend considerations to two spatial dimensions where we find both solitonic and vortical structures. The solitary waves localized in both directions are found to be spectrally stable. However, all other structures that we consider in this model, including line solitons -- which are homogeneous 2D extensions of 1D solitons -- and vortices of topological charge S=1 and S=2 are found to be spectrally unstable. The focal point of our studies then turns to the examination of the collisions of the stable two-dimensional solitary waves for which we map a two-parameter space of soliton speeds and frequencies, in terms of the potential outcomes. While the standard scenarios of merger, inelastic collision leading to separation, separation that leaves behind a localized pulse are all possible, the intriguing outcome that we highlight here is that of a longitudinal collision yielding a transverse spliting of the solitons, either with or without a localized pulse remnant.
summary: This paper analyzes solitary waves in a plasma-relevant Nonlinear Schrödinger equation with ponderomotive nonlinearity. It establishes that while certain complex structures are unstable, simple 2D solitons are stable enough to undergo collisions. The most notable finding is the prediction of transverse splitting during longitudinal soliton collisions.
main_problem: The study investigates the stability and collision dynamics of solitary waves and vortices governed by a Nonlinear Schrödinger equation incorporating ponderomotive nonlinearity.
main_result: Stable solitary waves are found in both 1D and 2D, while line solitons and vortices ($S=1, S=2$) are spectrally unstable. Collisions can result in merger, dispersion, or an intriguing transverse splitting of the solitons.
method: The analysis combines spectral stability theory (using perturbation methods) with numerical simulations of head-on collisions using high-order Runge-Kutta integrators.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a Nonlinear Schrödinger equation featuring ponderomotive nonlinearity, relevant for self-trapped laser beams in plasma. The analysis extends from 1D stationary solutions to full 2D structures like radial and vortex solitons.
key_observables: Soliton speed ($c$), oscillation frequency ($\omega$), topological charge ($S$), spectral growth rates ($\lambda$), and density split ratio ($R$).
important_parameters: The parameters governing the nonlinearity strength, wave number components ($k_	heta, k_y$), and collision velocities/frequencies are crucial for determining the outcome.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific forms for perturbations to test stability and focuses on head-on collisions of non-topological, spectrally stable solitons.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate profiles of 1D, radial, and vortex solitons; diagrams map out collision regimes in the $(\omega, c)$ plane (e.g., trapping, dispersion); and power density plots show the evolution during specific collisions or instability growth.
paper_structure: The paper systematically moves from establishing the governing equation and finding stationary solutions to performing detailed spectral stability analyses for different soliton types, culminating in extensive numerical simulations of collision dynamics across various parameter regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a rich theoretical framework for understanding nonlinear wave interactions (solitons) in physical media like plasmas, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and nonlinear wave physics often studied alongside AMO topics.
